Prealgebra · Lesson 4.3

Multiplying and Dividing Fractions

Solve this lesson →All lessons

A baker gives her apprentice 1331​ of a dough strip, and he uses half of that for a braid. The braid is a part of a part, so it is smaller than either piece. What single fraction of the whole strip is it?

Problem
A garden bed has 1212 equal squares, and 2332​ are covered. Split 1212 into 33 groups, keep 22. How many squares end up covered?
Show a hint
  • The bottom number of 2332​ tells you how many equal groups to split the 12 squares into. Make the groups first, before you worry about how many to keep.
Show the full solution
The bottom number 3 says split the 12 squares into three equal groups, and 12÷3=412÷3=4, so each group is 4 squares. The top number 2 says keep two of those groups, which is 2×4=82×4=8 squares. 88​ That matches 23×12=243=832​×12=324​=8. The word of works exactly like a multiply sign.
Problem
One batch needs 5885​ cup of cherries, and 66 batches are made. Compute 6×586×85​. Leave your answer as an improper fraction.
Show a hint
  • Six batches means you lay down 5885​ of a cup, then another 5885​, and so on, 6 times over. The eighths are all the same size, so think about how many eighths you end up with once you have collected 6 of these scoops.
  • Write the 6 as 6116​ and multiply straight across, tops times tops and bottoms times bottoms. The bottom stays 8 because each scoop is still an eighth of a cup, only the count of eighths changed. So you get 6×51×81×86×5​, then simplify.
Show the full solution
Each batch takes 5 eighths of a cup, so 6 batches take 6×5=306×5=30 eighths. Written out, 61×58=30816​×85​=830​, and both numbers share a factor of 2, so the total is 15/415/4​ The bottom stays 8 the whole way. Collecting eighths changes how many you have, not how big each one is.
Problem
A worker uses 1441​ of a netting roll, then patches 1331​ of that panel. The patch is 11 cell in the grid of equal cells. Write it as a/ba/b of the whole roll.
Show a hint
  • You do not need to multiply anything yet, just count slivers. Each of the 4 equal panels gets cut into 3 equal slivers. Lay the slivers end to end down the whole roll and count how many there are in total.
  • There are 4×3=124×3=12 equal slivers covering the whole roll, and they are all the same size. Her patch is one of those 12 equal pieces, so it is one part out of 12 of the whole.
Show the full solution
She uses 1331​ of 1441​ of the roll. Cutting each of the 4 panels into 3 slivers makes 4×3=124×3=12 equal slivers across the whole roll, and her patch is one of them. 1/121/12​ Taking 1aa1​ of 1bb1​ always gives 1abab1​, because the second cut multiplies the number of pieces.
Problem
A 3×53×5 mosaic: pale glass fills 22 of 33 columns, and gold fills 33 of 55 rows. What fraction of the panel does the overlap cover? Reduce fully, write as a/ba/b.
Show a hint
  • The grid is 33 columns wide and 55 rows tall, so the whole panel is cut into 3×53×5 equal cells. The overlap is the block that is both in the pale 22 columns and in the gold 33 rows. How many columns wide is that block, and how many rows tall? Those two counts are the tops of your fractions.
  • Multiply tops with tops and bottoms with bottoms. Two thirds of three fifths is 23×35=2×33×5=61532​×53​=3×52×3​=156​. Now find gcd⁡(6,15)gcd(6,15) and divide both numbers by it.
Show the full solution
The panel is cut into 3×5=153×5=15 equal cells. The overlap is 2 columns wide and 3 rows tall, so it holds 2×3=62×3=6 cells, giving 23×35=61532​×53​=156​. Dividing top and bottom by 3 gives 2/52/5​ That is why multiplying fractions multiplies tops and bottoms. The tops count how wide and tall the overlap is, and the bottoms count how the whole square was cut up.
Key idea
Multiplying two fractions. Multiply the tops for the new top and the bottoms for the new bottom, so ab×cd=a×cb×dba​×dc​=b×da×c​. On a grid, the new top counts the overlap block (cells across times cells up) and the new bottom counts the whole square (columns times rows). Taking a fraction of an amount is this same multiplication, and a whole number counts as itself over 11. Two proper fractions always multiply to something smaller than both, because a part of a part is less than either one.
Problem
Compute 1415×25211514​×2125​: prime-factor each number, cancel any prime appearing in a top and a bottom, multiply what remains. Fully reduced result as a/ba/b?
Show a hint
  • Before you multiply anything, look across the two fractions for shared factors. The 14 on top and the 21 on the bottom both hold a 7. The 25 on top and the 15 on the bottom both hold a 5. A factor on any top cancels with the same factor on any bottom, no matter which fraction it sits in.
  • Write it as 2⋅73⋅5×5⋅53⋅73⋅52⋅7​×3⋅75⋅5​. Cross out the matching 77 (from 14 and 21) and one matching 55 (from 25 and 15). What survives on top is 2⋅52⋅5 and on the bottom is 3⋅33⋅3. Multiply each side.
Show the full solution
Break each number into primes. 14=2⋅714=2⋅7, 25=5⋅525=5⋅5, 15=3⋅515=3⋅5, and 21=3⋅721=3⋅7, so the product is 2⋅73⋅5×5⋅53⋅7=2⋅7⋅5⋅53⋅5⋅3⋅7.3⋅52⋅7​×3⋅75⋅5​=3⋅5⋅3⋅72⋅7⋅5⋅5​. The 77s cancel and one 55 cancels, leaving 2⋅5=102⋅5=10 on top and 3⋅3=93⋅3=9 on the bottom. 10/910/9​ Multiplying first gives 350315315350​, the same answer after much more reducing. In a product of fractions every top factor is paired against every bottom factor, so cancel before you multiply.
Problem
34×45×56×6743​×54​×65​×76​: each bottom is the next top. Most cancel. What single reduced fraction remains?
Show a hint
  • Do not multiply the tops into one giant number and the bottoms into another. Instead, write all four numerators on one line over all four denominators on one line, like 3×4×5×64×5×6×74×5×6×73×4×5×6​, and then hunt for numbers that appear in both rows.
  • A factor on top cancels the same factor on the bottom. The 44 shows up on top and on bottom, so it vanishes. So does the 55. So does the 66. Cross all three pairs out and read off whatever is still standing on top and on bottom.
Show the full solution
Stack all four tops over all four bottoms, 34×45×56×67=3×4×5×64×5×6×7.43​×54​×65​×76​=4×5×6×73×4×5×6​. The 44, the 55, and the 66 each sit on top and on the bottom, so all three pairs cancel and leave   37  73​​ Only the first top and the last bottom have no partner to cancel against. Everything in the middle was both a top and a bottom, so it washed out.
Fun fact
A telescoping product collapses like a folding spyglass. Each bottom matched the next top, cancelled, and left only the first top and last bottom standing.
Key idea
Cancel before you multiply. In a product of fractions, the tops all multiply into one top and the bottoms into one bottom. If a top and a bottom share a factor, divide both by it first, even if they sit in different fractions. Clearing shared factors early keeps the numbers small and gives an answer already in simplest form. In a long chain each bottom often cancels the next top, so the product telescopes to the first top over the last bottom.

Multiplying by a proper fraction makes things smaller. Division goes the other way and asks how many small pieces fit inside a big one, which is multiplication run backward. The tool that turns a division back into a multiplication is the reciprocal.

Problem
A machine scales by 712127​, and a second machine must undo it so the combined product is 11. What fraction times 712127​ gives 11? Write as a/ba/b.
Show a hint
  • Multiplying fractions multiplies the tops together and the bottoms together. For the result to be 11, the top of the product and the bottom of the product have to come out equal. Picture what the second fraction's top and bottom would need to be so that the 77 and the 1212 end up matched.
  • The 77 sits on top of 712127​, so to cancel it you need a 77 on the bottom of your fraction. The 1212 sits on the bottom, so to cancel it you need a 1212 on top. Put those together.
Show the full solution
Flip 712127​ upside down to get 127712​. Then 712×127=8484=1127​×712​=8484​=1, exactly what the second machine needs. 12/712/7​ A fraction equals 11 when its top and bottom match, and swapping the two numbers guarantees that. The flipped partner is called the reciprocal.
Key idea
Reciprocal. The reciprocal of a fraction has the numerator and denominator swapped, so the reciprocal of abba​ is baab​. A fraction times its reciprocal is always 11, because the product has a×ba×b on top and a×ba×b on the bottom, and any number over itself is 11. Each of 11 and −1−1 is its own reciprocal, and 00 has no reciprocal, the same reason you can never divide by 00.
Problem
Five builders share a 33 m plank: 3÷5=3×153÷5=3×51​. How long is each share in meters? Write as a/ba/b.
Show a hint
  • Splitting the plank into five equal pieces and keeping one piece is exactly taking one fifth of the plank. So instead of 3÷53÷5, you can ask what is 1551​ of 33 meters.
  • Taking 1551​ of something means multiplying by 1551​, so each share is 3×153×51​. Multiply the 33 by the top of the fraction and keep the 55 on the bottom.
Show the full solution
Sharing 3 meters among 5 builders is 3÷53÷5, and splitting into 5 equal parts and keeping one is taking 1551​ of the plank. So each share is 3×153×51​, which is three fifth-meter pieces. 3/53/5​ Dividing by a whole number is multiplying by its reciprocal, so a÷ba÷b is just the fraction abba​.
Problem
A 55 L carboy is poured into 1331​ L jars. One liter fills 33 jars, and the carboy holds 55 liters. How many 1331​ L jars does the full carboy fill?
Show a hint
  • Forget the division symbol for a second and just count. Each single liter breaks into how many of these little third liter jars? Then you have 5 whole liters to pour, not just one.
  • Three thirds fit in every liter, so one liter fills 33 jars. With 55 liters lined up, you fill 55 groups of 33 jars. Multiply 5×35×3.
Show the full solution
One liter splits into 3 jars, since 13+13+13=131​+31​+31​=1. With 5 liters lined up, that is 5×3=155×3=15​ jars. The question is 5÷135÷31​, and the answer came out bigger than the 5 we started with. Dividing by a number below 11 always does that, since many small pieces fit.
Problem
A trim piece is 5665​ m. You want pieces of 2992​ m each. Keep the first fraction, flip the divisor, and multiply. What is 56÷2965​÷92​ in lowest terms?
Show a hint
  • Only the divisor flips. The 5665​ stays exactly as it is, and 2992​ turns into 9229​. Now the ÷÷ becomes a ××, so you are really finding 56×9265​×29​.
  • Before you multiply across, look for a shared factor. The 99 on top and the 66 on the bottom both have a factor of 33, so the 99 becomes 33 and the 66 becomes 22. Then multiply straight across, 5×35×3 over 2×22×2.
Show the full solution
Keep the first fraction and flip the divisor, so 56÷29=56×9265​÷92​=65​×29​. The 99 and the 66 share a factor of 33, turning them into 33 and 22, so the product is 5×32×2=15/42×25×3​=15/4​ That is 334343​, so three whole pieces fit with three quarters of another left over.
Key idea
To divide by a fraction, flip it and multiply. Dividing by a number counts how many copies of it fit inside. Splitting something into bb equal shares and keeping one is taking 1bb1​ of it, and the same swap works for any fraction, so a÷pq=a×qpa÷qp​=a×pq​. The flip also recovers a whole from a part. If pqqp​ of a number is kk, the number is k×qpk×pq​. Dividing by a number smaller than 11 makes the answer bigger, since many small copies fit inside.
Problem
A fundraiser raised 3232 (thousands). That is 2332​ of the goal. What is the full goal, in thousands?
Show a hint
  • You are not asked for two thirds of something here. You already know the two thirds part, it is the 32, and you are hunting for the whole. Dividing by a fraction is how you walk a multiplication backward, so think about 32÷2332÷32​.
  • Dividing by 2332​ is the same as multiplying by the flipped fraction 3223​. So compute 32×3232×23​, and notice the 32 and the 2 are ready to cancel before you multiply.
Show the full solution
The forward story is goal × 23=32×32​=32, so the goal is 32÷23=32×3232÷32​=32×23​. Cancel the 2 against the 32, since 32=16×232=16×2, which leaves 16×3=4816×3=48​ thousand. Checking forward, 48÷3=1648÷3=16 and 16×2=3216×2=32. Multiplying by the reciprocal is how you recover a whole from a part.
Problem
Feed 1212 into a machine: first multiply by 4994​, then divide by 815158​. What is the result?
Show a hint
  • Dividing by a fraction is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal. So the second setting, divide by 815158​, is really multiply by 158815​. Once both steps are multiplications, they collapse into one, because two multiplications in a row are just one multiplication by their product.
  • The single fraction is 49×15894​×815​. Before multiplying straight across, cancel across the fractions. The 44 and the 88 share a factor of 44, and the 1515 and the 99 share a factor of 33. That leaves 13×52=5631​×25​=65​. Now compute 12×5612×65​.
Show the full solution
Dividing by 815158​ is multiplying by 158815​, so the machine does 12×49×15812×94​×815​. Cancel first. The 44 and the 88 share a factor of 44, and the 1515 and the 99 share a factor of 33, so 49×158=1×53×2=56.94​×815​=3×21×5​=65​. Then 12×56=606=1012×65​=660​=10​ A multiply and a divide folded into one fraction. Chain as many of them as you like and the result is still just a fraction.
Fun fact
Percent = Latin per centum, and "30 percent of" always meant ×30100×10030​. Egyptians used reciprocals for 3000+ years, and the Rhind Papyrus is a long unit-fraction table.

Practice these ideas

Practice
3443​ of a parking lot is shaded, and 2992​ of shaded spaces are reserved. What fraction of the whole lot is shaded-reserved? Write in lowest terms as a/ba/b.
Show the solution
Two ninths of three quarters is 29×3492​×43​. Cancel first. The 33 on top and the 99 on the bottom share a 33, and the 22 on top and the 44 on the bottom share a 22, leaving 1×13×2=1/63×21×1​=1/6​ Without cancelling you get 636366​, which reduces to the same thing with more work.
Practice
Three quarters of 2020 students ride bikes. Split 2020 into 44 equal groups, keep three. How many students ride bikes?
Show the solution
Taking 3443​ of 20 means splitting 20 into four groups of 20÷4=520÷4=5 and keeping three of them, so 3×5=153×5=15​ students. As one multiplication it is 34×20=604=1543​×20=460​=15, the same answer either way.
Practice
Light through two panes: outer passes 2332​, and inner passes 6776​. Cancel 33 and 66 first. What fraction gets through?
Show the solution
The light through both panes is 23×6732​×76​. The 66 on top and the 33 on the bottom both divide by 33, giving 21×2712​×72​, and multiplying across gives 4/74/7​ Cancelling first kept the numbers small and left nothing to reduce at the end.
Practice
Each of 88 ornaments uses 310103​ m of wire. Total wire is 8×3108×103​. How many meters are needed? Give as an improper fraction a/ba/b in lowest terms.
Show the solution
Eight copies of 310103​ is 8×310=2410108×3​=1024​. Both numbers are even, so dividing each by 2 gives 12/512/5​ meters. Multiplying a fraction by a whole number scales the top only. The pieces stay tenths, you just have more of them.
Practice
Compute 914×712149​×127​. Cancel 77 from 77 and 1414, and 33 from 99 and 1212. What fraction a/ba/b in lowest terms do you get?
Show the solution
Cancel the crossing pairs first. The 77 and the 1414 share a 77, so they become 11 and 22. The 99 and the 1212 share a 33, so they become 33 and 44. The problem turns into 32×14.23​×41​. Now multiply straight across. The tops give 3×1=33×1=3 and the bottoms give 2×4=82×4=8, so the product is 3883​. Since gcd⁡(3,8)=1gcd(3,8)=1, it is already in lowest terms. 3/83/8​
Practice
A jug is 5885​ full. You pour off 2552​ of the juice inside. The two 55s cancel. What fraction of the full jug did you pour out?
Show the solution
Pouring off 2552​ of what is in the jug, while 5885​ is in there, is 25×5852​×85​. Instead of multiplying straight across into 10404010​ and reducing later, cancel first. The 5 on the bottom of 2552​ and the 5 on the top of 5885​ cancel to 1, leaving 21×18=2812​×81​=82​. One more pair, the 2 against the 8, gives 1441​. So you poured out 1/41/4​ of the full jug.
Practice
Chain: 45×56×67×7854​×65​×76​×87​. Most tops and bottoms cancel in pairs. What single fraction a/ba/b does the chain equal?
Show the solution
Collect all the tops over all the bottoms, 45×56×67×78=4×5×6×75×6×7×8.54​×65​×76​×87​=5×6×7×84×5×6×7​. The 55, the 66, and the 77 each appear on top and on the bottom, so those pairs cancel and leave 4884​, which reduces to 1/21/2​ Only the first top and the last bottom have no partner, which is what makes a chain like this telescope.
Practice
A stretch setting multiplies by 9449​. What single fraction a/ba/b multiplies with 9449​ to give exactly 11?
Show the solution
Flip 9449​ to get 4994​. Checking, 94×49=3636=149​×94​=3636​=1, so the flip really does undo the stretch. 4/94/9​ Two numbers that multiply to 11 are reciprocals, and for a fraction the reciprocal is always the same two numbers swapped.
Practice
A 44 L drum is emptied with a 1331​ L dispenser. How many full pumps empty the drum?
Show the solution
One liter holds 3 of the third-liter pumps, and there are 4 liters, so 4×3=124×3=12​ pumps. That count is 4÷134÷31​, and dividing by 1331​ is the same as multiplying by 33.
Practice
A tank is 710107​ full. Each truck carries 1221​ of a full tank. How many truckloads does the current water fill? Give as a/ba/b in lowest terms.
Show the solution
Counting truckloads is 710÷12107​÷21​. Flip the divisor and multiply, 710×21=1410107​×12​=1014​, and dividing top and bottom by 22 gives 7/57/5​ A little more than one half-tank should come out, and 7557​ sits just past 11.
Practice
Tray A holds 10212110​ of a ream, and Tray B holds 514145​. Compute 1021÷5142110​÷145​ and give the result as a/ba/b in lowest terms.
Show the solution
Flip the divisor, so 1021÷514=1021×1452110​÷145​=2110​×514​. The 1010 and the 55 share a factor of 55, and the 1414 and the 2121 share a factor of 77, which leaves 23×2132​×12​. 4/34/3​ Straight across it would be 140105105140​, and since gcd⁡(140,105)=35gcd(140,105)=35 that reduces to the same thing.
Practice
Priya is 3553​ through her novel, which is 2727 pages. Since 3553​ of the whole =27=27, multiply 2727 by 5335​. How many pages total?
Show the solution
Three fifths of the total is 27, so the total is 27÷35=27×5327÷53​=27×35​. The 33 on the bottom divides the 2727, leaving 9×5=459×5=45​ pages. Checking, 35×45=2753​×45=27. Multiplying by the reciprocal is how you get a whole back from a part.
Practice
A spool holds 154415​ m, and each bow needs 3883​ m. Compute 154÷38415​÷83​. How many whole bows does the ribbon make?
Show the solution
Flip 3883​ to 8338​, so 154÷38=154×83415​÷83​=415​×38​. The 88 and the 44 share a factor of 44, and the 1515 and the 33 share a factor of 33, leaving 51×21=1015​×12​=10​ The quotient is a whole number, so the ribbon divides evenly with nothing left over.
Practice
Five eighths of a 2424 g block is measured out and split into jars of 3443​ g each. How many jars does the merchant fill?
Show the solution
She measures out 24×5824×85​ grams. Since 24÷8=324÷8=3, that is 3×5=153×5=15 grams. Splitting 15 grams into 3443​ gram jars is 15÷34=15×43=603=2015÷43​=15×34​=360​=20​ jars. The two steps pull opposite ways. Multiplying by a fraction under 11 shrank the amount, then dividing by one grew the count back up.
Practice
Three filters: 56×67×7865​×76​×87​. The chain telescopes. Divide that result by 5885​. What single number is the answer?
Show the solution
The three filters give 5×6×76×7×86×7×85×6×7​, and the 66 and the 77 each cancel top against bottom, leaving 5885​. Dividing by 5885​ means multiplying by 8558​, and 58×85=404085​×58​=4040​. 11​ Any nonzero fraction times its own reciprocal is 11, and here the surviving signal was exactly the baseline.
